judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble is a definite identification of two named parties with defined terms "Party"/"Parties" and an express incorporation of Exhibit I definitions; nothing in the wording carries a second reasonable meaning, though "by and among" is loose for a two-party deal.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It names only Licensee and Clearwire, yet Article V's reps run "to Clearwire and Clearwire Parent," Section 6.01–6.02 give reps of Clearwire Parent, Section 7.02 imposes notice duties on Clearwire Parent, and Section 4.02(c)(iii)(2) speaks of "each Clearwire Affiliate that is a Party hereto" — a real question whether Clearwire Parent is bound.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals define key operative terms (FCC Licenses, MHzPops, Commercial Spectrum Capacity, Total Consideration) in narrative form, and the "but for all of the elements of the Total Consideration" language is an interpretive lever rather than a plainly ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "EBS Economic Royalties" and "Total Consideration" appear nowhere in the operative text (Article II uses "Prepaid Royalties" and "Economic Royalties"), and the recital that the deal is a bundle sits awkwardly against Section 2.02's full-refund mechanic and Section 9.01's short Term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is a descriptive overview defining "EBS Spectrum Capacity" as Initial plus Future Spectrum Capacity "when under IUA hereunder"; the parenthetical qualifier is slightly awkward but its meaning is discernible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section 1.02(a)–(b) and Article IV's IUA closing mechanics; I found no provision it contradicts, only the general definitional overlap with the recitals.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The acknowledgment that the payment "exceeds the value of the Initial Spectrum Capacity" and "includes additional consideration for the Option and the ROFR" plus "an advance payment toward Future Spectrum Capacity" does not allocate any amount between those characterisations, leaving the payment's legal character contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits in real tension with Section 2.02 and Section 9.01, which require refund of the entire unapplied Prepaid Royalties Balance on any expiration or termination — including, apparently, the portion this clause says was consideration for the Option and ROFR.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The phrase "which consists of, among other items" introduces four enumerated Access Right Royalties plus "technology, facilities, equipment and other functionality," a classic general-catch-all-against-specifics problem about the bundle's outer reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article III in fact lists more items than the four named (MVNO resale, device access, feature sharing), so the enumeration is under-inclusive relative to Article III, though the "among other items" saver largely harmonises them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause identifies the exchange and labels the Article III bundle "Access Right Royalties"; apart from OCR artefacts it is a definite cross-referencing sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section 2.01, Article III and Article IV; the only friction is that Section 1.01(c) already used the same defined term, which is duplication rather than conflict.
judgments.clause_name: Section 1.02(a) IUAs for Initial Spectrum Capacity

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Central terms are indeterminate: "Available" spectrum, "prices to be negotiated in good faith based on the fair market value," and a cap that is both a ceiling and the negotiation subject — an option whose price term is an agreement to agree is precisely what parties fight over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with Section 1.04's ROFR, Section 2.02's refund proviso keyed to "the Option periods described in Section 1.02(b)," and Section 9.01's 18-month Term, and whether an unexercised Option keeps the Term (and the $23 million) alive is not resolved by reading them together.
judgments.clause_name: Section 1.02(b) — Option for Future Spectrum Capacity

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition contains a mechanical error — "a GSA the covers the same metropolitan are in Puerto Rico" — and the MFN machinery layers "Higher Price," a $0.15 ceiling and a $0.10 floor with an illustrative example whose scope (adjacent and overlapping GSAs) is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its twelve-month post-Term tail and the Puerto Rico carve-out in Section 9.01 ("except as it pertains to Puerto Rico") and Section 1.02(d) create a Term-and-survival puzzle across three provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two sentences pull against each other within the same subsection: PR Options survive "without regard to the earlier expiration of the Term," while "[a]ny outstanding Options shall lapse automatically upon the expiration of the Term" except where prior notice was given.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.03 says Option rights survive termination if the triggering event occurred before termination, and Section 2.02 suspends Term expiration while Option periods run — three provisions giving different answers to when Options die.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The covenant to "cause the entity providing each of the Access Right Royalties" to assume obligations and be jointly and severally liable is definite, though "Service Affiliate" is defined circularly by reference to whoever performs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Section 1.01(a)'s reference to Collateral Documents and the Article III delivery obligations, and the last sentence expressly preserves Clearwire's primary obligation, avoiding conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[B]ona fide written offer ... that Licensee desires to accept" and the cash-equivalence machinery for non-cash consideration are workable but leave judgment calls; the opening double condition (unless (1) and (2)) is convoluted about when the ROFR applies at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly meshes with Section 1.02(b) and refers disputes to "arbitration under this Agreement," but the only dispute mechanism (Section 10.11) is truncated in the instrument, leaving the arbitration reference unsupported.
judgments.clause_name: Section 1.04 Right of First Refusal on IUAs

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The payment obligation is a fixed dollar amount payable on execution with a defined term "Prepaid Royalties"; the wording is about as definite as a payment clause gets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The section heading calls these "Economic Royalties" while the recitals call them "EBS Economic Royalties" and Section 1.01(b) characterises the same sum as partly Option/ROFR consideration and partly an advance — a characterisation problem for Section 2.02's refund.
judgments.clause_name: Section 2.01 EBS Spectrum Capacity Economic Royalties

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso that "the Term shall not be deemed to have expired for this purpose during a period that the Option periods described in Section 1.02(b) have not terminated" is opaque, and the final sentence extends the Term whenever Clearwire extends the refund date, giving Clearwire an open-ended unilateral extension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This directly grinds against Section 9.01, which fixes the Term at 18 months and forbids extension "beyond the first to occur of the events described in clauses (2) or (3)" — one of which is the very refund this section defers; the two cannot easily be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]ommercially reasonable best efforts" to "(in good faith) consider" a joint venture, conditioned on the venture involving purchases "at greater than Clearwire's lowest wholesale price," is a promise whose content and trigger are both vague; the third-party-consistency sentence adds a second undefined benchmark.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is broadly consistent with Section 3.05's lowest-wholesale-rate pricing and Section 1.01(c), though the "manner consistent with ... third parties" standard could cut against the specific entitlements in Sections 3.03–3.04.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence signposting provision entitling Licensee to accounts "as provided in" three named sections; there is nothing to construe on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It accurately cross-references Sections 3.02–3.04 and is consistent with Section 1.01(c)'s bundle description.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]he same capacity and characteristics as the highest level of premium mass market retail service" and "associated with an Educational End User at the time" are elastic benchmarks, and the Acceptable Use Policy is Clearwire's own and changeable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section 3.05(a), which builds MVNO accounts on this definition, and with Section 3.04(a)(ii)'s Educational End User restriction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[I]n such locations served by the Clearwire National Platform on a full time basis as Licensee desires for its operations" is broadly worded, and the FCC-change mechanism (jointly approach the FCC, then dispute resolution) is definite in structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to "the Dispute Resolution Procedure," which in this instrument (Section 10.11) is cut off mid-sentence, and "Clearwire may not use the Educational Reservation" must be squared with Clearwire's broad access rights under the IUAs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The upward adjustment applies to "[t]he number of Cost-Free Educational Accounts" without saying whether it means only Basic accounts or all accounts, and "average throughput" measurement is left to later agreement or arbitration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The five-year proportionate adjustment here sits against Section 3.04(a)'s annual January 31 recalculation of Additional accounts, and the per-Cell-Site metric here against the per-Sector metric there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short introductory sentence with "[i]n addition to, and not in lieu of" language that makes the additive intent explicit and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It characterises the Section 3.03 accounts as provided "pursuant to the Educational Reservation," whereas Section 3.03(b) describes Basic accounts as a Clearwire deliverable distinct from the 5% reservation — a mild mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The greater-of formula is mechanically stated, but "Sector" and "Market Area" carry the weight of the calculation and the annual recalculation date is fixed, so the wording is largely determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The per-Sector floor and annual recalculation must be reconciled with Section 3.03(b)'s per-Cell-Site count adjusted every five years, and with Section 3.04(b)'s launch-based delivery timing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The subsection is mislabelled "(3)" where the scheme requires "(i)," and the Local Channel Ratio denominator ("channels with substantially overlapping GSAs then used to provide service ... licensed to or under a use agreement with Clearwire") is a measurement definition with genuine boundary uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.08(b) cross-refers to "Sections 3.04(a)(i1)" and Section 3.04(a) refers to "the Formula Quantity," so the numbering slip creates a small referencing problem but no substantive conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[O]fficially associated with such Educational End User" and "involved in university matters" are vague boundary terms, softened but not cured by the illustrative example.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section 3.05's limited resale right and Section 3.08(b)'s no-resale covenant, which expressly carve back to this subsection.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger — commercial launch in a Market Area, or the Commencement Date if later — is a definite two-part timing rule; the self-reference "pursuant to this Section 3.04(b)" is redundant but harmless.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aligns with Section 3.01's "from and after the Commencement Date of an IUA" and with Section 3.04(a); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]he lowest wholesale rate provided by Clearwire to an arms-length third party in such Market Area or other comparable market pursuant to any applicable agreement" leaves both the comparator market and the qualifying agreement open to argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 2x cap keyed to "the number of Cost-Free Educational Accounts" depends on whether that means Basic, Additional or both under Sections 3.03(b) and 3.04(a) — a quantifiable knock-on ambiguity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ny Licensee" is a mechanical slip in a single-licensee agreement, and "thirty (30) days after the availability of such services" does not identify whose availability or of what.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers to a "standard Clearwire wholesale agreement form ... consistent with the terms of this Agreement," which fits Section 1.03's Collateral Document machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "10% above Clearwire's cost to acquire such end-user equipment" is a definite pricing formula; "cost to acquire" could arguably include or exclude overhead, but the term is narrow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The no-resale restriction here matches Section 3.04(a)(ii) and Section 3.08(b); no inconsistency appears.
judgments.clause_name: Section 3.06 Access to Educational End User Devices

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision stacks vague qualifiers — "generally provided," "reasonably necessary support," "customers generally" — and refers to "their agreement" with no identified antecedent, a mechanical slip in a materially important entitlement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 3.08(a)'s premium-content-provider parity and Section 3.08(c)'s capacity carve-back, which qualify but do not contradict it.
judgments.clause_name: Section 3.07 Sharing of Features and Service Sets

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]he same degree of access to, and use of, any system capability, service or feature set that is provided to premium third party content providers" turns on the undefined class "premium third party content providers."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is qualified by Section 3.08(c) and overlaps Section 3.07's parity right; the two parity standards are cumulative rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Clearwire's most favored program suppliers" and "equal features and/or service sets" are comparison terms without a defined comparator set, and the cross-reference is mistyped as "3.04(a)(i1)."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The no-resale covenant expressly excepts Sections 3.04(a)(ii) and 3.05, so it harmonises with the MVNO right rather than conflicting with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[N]o longer commercially and technically feasible due to limitations in network capabilities" is a broad unilateral escape from a bargained entitlement, and the reservation is drafted entirely in Clearwire's favour.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directs that "Clearwire shall comply with the provisions of ARTICLE III to ensure timely access to information about capacity usage," but Article III contains no capacity-information provision — a cross-reference that cannot be made good on the face of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]ommercially reasonable best efforts" is an internally mixed standard, and "one ordinary unpaid channel carried on such entity's basic tier" plus "incremental out-of-pocket costs ... exclusively for the benefit of Licensee" are all soft-edged.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is one of the four bundle elements named in Section 1.01(c) and is consistent with it; nothing else in the instrument contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short instruction that each party take "the following actions required of it by subsections (a) through (c)"; the drafting is definite though the singular "it" is loose for two parties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It correctly frames Sections 4.01(a)–(c) and is consistent with Section 4.02(a)'s Initial Closing on the Effective Date.
judgments.clause_name: Section 4.01 Deliveries at Execution of this Agreement

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The delivery list is specific and closed; "each a 'Wire Account'" is a plural artefact against a single specified account, a minor mechanical looseness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires delivery under "Schedule 4.01" and "Exhibit III," but the instrument's List of Schedules names only Schedule A and the Licensee Schedule, so the referenced schedule is absent from the document as constituted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of Clearwire deliverables is specific, but "the Upfront Royalty provided for in the applicable EBS Spectrum Capacity IUA as reflected on Schedule A" uses an undefined term for the money changing hands at closing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The relationship between the "Upfront Royalty" here and the $23,000,000 "Prepaid Royalties" of Section 2.01 (applied against IUA amounts under Section 1.02(b)) is not spelled out, leaving the payment architecture in some doubt.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard closing-certificate requirement identifying two specific documents; the wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the certificate conditions in Sections 4.02(c)(ii)(2) and (iii)(2) and the certificate exhibits listed at the front.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]he closing of the transactions provided in this Agreement, including with respect to IUAs ... executed on the date hereof (each an 'Initial Closing')" ties the closing to a fixed date and is determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Table of Contents numbers this material as Section 4.03 while the text numbers it 4.02, and no Section 4.02 appears in the TOC — a numbering divergence across the instrument that Section 10.05 partly neutralises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Subsequent Closing occurs "when the Parties reach agreement on the pricing," which is definite as a mechanic even though the underlying agreement may never occur.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with Section 1.02(b)'s negotiation process and Section 10.02's survival keyed to Subsequent Closing Dates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lead-in promises "the following condition" and then the condition itself is a verbless fragment ("No temporary restraining order ... preventing the consummation"), a mechanical defect in an operative closing condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section 4.04's further-assurances duty and with the party-specific conditions that follow.
judgments.clause_name: Section 4.02(c)(i) Conditions to Each Party's Obligations at a Closing

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clearwire's conditions are two specific, closed items with an express written-waiver requirement; the wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels Section 4.02(c)(iii) and is consistent with Article V's reps; no conflict identified.
judgments.clause_name: Section 4.02(c)(ii) Conditions to the Obligations of Clearwire

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The subsection is mislabelled "(ii)" although it follows another "(ii)," and it requires board resolutions of "each Clearwire Affiliate that is a Party hereto" when no affiliate signs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That reference to Clearwire Affiliates as Parties cannot be reconciled with the preamble, which names only Licensee and Clearwire, and echoes the Clearwire Parent problem in Article VI.
judgments.clause_name: Section 4.02(c)(iii) Conditions to Obligations of Licensee

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, concrete logistics provision naming a specific law firm's office for the Initial Closing; nothing is left open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section 4.02(a) and the notice addresses in Section 10.06.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[R]easonable best efforts" and "necessary, proper or advisable" are standard but genuinely open-textured, though the clause is subordinate to the Agreement's express terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 7.01's commercially-reasonable-efforts covenant, a slight difference in standard but not a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional organisation and good-standing rep with materiality carve-out; "as proposed to be conducted" is a modest expansion but a familiar and workable one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It excepts matters "disclosed in Schedule 5.01," a schedule not listed in the instrument's List of Schedules, which is a documentary gap rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard authorisation and enforceability rep with the usual bankruptcy and equity qualifiers; its wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines "Licensee Documents" as those delivered "on the date hereof," which is narrower than Section 8.01(a)'s indemnity for certificates delivered "pursuant to this Agreement," a small scope difference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause contains OCR/typographic slips in its romanettes and says the transaction will not "create in any Party the rights to accelerate," using the capitalised defined term where a third person is plainly meant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section 6.03(a)'s mirror rep and with the Schedule 5.03 carve-out structure; no substantive conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[E]xcept as contemplated herein or therein" is an undefined saver that could swallow the rep, since what is "contemplated" is itself a question of construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clearwire's mirror rep in Section 6.03(b) expressly carves out FCC spectrum-lease applications, while this Licensee rep contains no comparable FCC carve-out even though the IUAs require FCC approval — an asymmetry that must be reconciled with Section 7.05.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[N]or ... does there exist any basis therefore" is extremely broad, and the closing exception for "immaterial claims brought against Licensee in the ordinary course of business" is a vague boundary sitting against the enumerated FCC Proceedings carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses simple "knowledge" while Section 5.05 uses "best knowledge" and Section 5.07 defines only the latter, leaving the standard for this rep unaddressed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is a thicket: an opening schedule exception, a "only to the best knowledge" qualifier, an assumption about third parties' compliance, then "has complied in all respects" immediately cut back by a Material Adverse Effect proviso — the interaction of "all respects" and the MAE carve-out is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.02 strips knowledge and Material Adverse Effect qualifiers when measuring Damages, which materially reworks the effect of the qualifiers built into this rep.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, absolute negative rep about brokers with no qualifier or catch-all; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Section 6.06 and is consistent with the indemnity structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition builds in "commercially reasonable investigation" twice and imputes facts Licensee "should have known," a constructive-knowledge standard whose reach is arguable but stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines only "best knowledge of Licensee," leaving Section 5.04's plain "knowledge of Licensee" and Clearwire's knowledge qualifiers in Sections 6.04–6.05 without an equivalent definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional organisation rep, definite as to states of organisation and entity types, with the usual MAE carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gives a representation of Clearwire Parent, a person the preamble does not make a Party, so who is liable for its breach under Section 8.01(b) (which indemnifies for "any representation or warranty of Clearwire set forth in ARTICLE VI") is unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard authorisation and enforceability language; the wording itself is settled boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states that "[e]ach of Clearwire Parent and Clearwire" has authority and defines "Clearwire Documents" accordingly, yet only Clearwire executes under the preamble and Section 6.03(a) speaks of Clearwire alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Aside from OCR artefacts in the romanettes, this is a conventional no-conflict rep with an MAE carve-out for clauses (ii) and (iii).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It addresses only Clearwire while Sections 6.01–6.02 also speak for Clearwire Parent, an asymmetry within Article VI itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rep is definite and its single exception — FCC spectrum lease applications — is specifically identified rather than left to a catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section 7.05's compliance covenant and with the IUA closing mechanics in Section 4.02.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A litigation rep with a materiality lead-in tied to "the ability of Clearwire to close hereunder"; the standard is narrow and stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is narrower than Licensee's Section 5.04 rep, but asymmetry between mirror reps is a bargained difference, not an incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[H]as complied in all respects" immediately qualified by an MAE carve-out creates the same all-respects/materiality tension as its Licensee counterpart, and the FCC carve-out is appended after a stray double comma.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.02's stripping of MAE and knowledge qualifiers for damages purposes reworks this rep's carve-outs, the same interaction as in Section 5.05.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat negative broker rep with no qualifiers; there is nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Section 5.06 and fits the indemnity scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Both sentences use "commercially reasonable efforts" to obtain unspecified consents "required to be obtained by Clearwire and the Licensee," and the second sentence's "its respective" is a grammatical slip for a single party.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with Sections 5.03(b), 6.03(b) and 7.05 on FCC filings; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger is subjective — notice is owed of any matter the party itself "determines is reasonably likely to constitute a breach" — which effectively conditions the duty on the obligor's own judgment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It imposes obligations on Clearwire Parent, which the preamble does not make a Party, repeating the Article VI mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[K]nowingly or negligently," "material risk," and a chain of provisos that shift expense to Clearwire and then excuse Licensee where the loss is caused "in whole or in part" by Clearwire, leave the covenant's real content contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The clause is expressly limited to spectrum "not ... subject to an IUA" yet is framed "subject to Clearwire's obligation to cause Licensee's FCC License to timely meet the substantial service requirement" — an obligation found nowhere in this Agreement, only in the IUAs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence conditions assignment on an assignee "reasonably acceptable to Clearwire," while the final "[n]otwithstanding the foregoing" sentence lets Licensee transfer "this Agreement or any of its rights or obligations" to controlled affiliates without consent — a scope tension within the same section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.09 speaks only of "permitted assigns" without a general assignment clause, and Section 1.04 applies the ROFR to "all Spectrum held by Licensee or any of its Affiliates," so a consent-free affiliate transfer interacts awkwardly with those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The compliance undertaking is definite; the second sentence records a belief and a covenant "not to express any contrary view," which is unusual but clear in its terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 3.03(a)'s process for jointly approaching the FCC and with the FCC carve-outs in Sections 6.03(b) and 6.05; no direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ll fees and taxes (now existing or hereafter arising) imposed on Licensee as a result of the licensing, regulation or use of Licensee's EBS Spectrum" followed by "including, without limitation" three examples is a general-then-specific structure whose outer reach is open, and "EBS Spectrum" is not the defined term used elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps Section 10.01's tax indemnity (sales, use, transfer and similar taxes "in connection with the Transactions") without either clause acknowledging the other, and its duration runs to the last IUA's expiry, well beyond the Section 9.01 Term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The covenant to "act in a cooperative manner to preserve the intent of the relationships" and use "commercially reasonable best efforts to maintain that mutual advantage in accordance with the initial intent of the Parties" is an aspirational standard with no ascertainable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to "the term of the IUAs," a much longer horizon than the 18-month Term in Section 9.01, but as a general good-faith gloss it does not contradict any specific provision.
judgments.clause_name: Section 7.07 Best Efforts for Duration of Relationship

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (iii) — Damages "otherwise related to the activities of Clearwire, any of its Affiliates or any of its sublicensees or resellers including, without limitation, damage to health" — is an open-ended catch-all following narrower specifics, the classic ejusdem generis problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.03 keys the deductible only to Sections 8.01(a)(i) and (b)(i), leaving limb (iii) uncapped and unthresholded, which fits the drafting but invites argument about whether that was intended.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Damages" is defined by a sprawling list closed with "of every kind and description, contingent or otherwise," which includes items (statutory compliance requirements, contingent liabilities) whose measurement is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its second sentence deliberately overrides the materiality and knowledge qualifiers written into Articles V and VI, a designed override that nonetheless creates tension with those reps as drafted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is titled and framed as a limit on liability for representation and warranty breaches, yet its operative text also mentions "the breach of any covenant," which the referenced subsections do not cover — a drafting mismatch about whether covenant claims are subject to the deductible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Section 8.01(a)(ii)/(b)(ii), which cover covenant breaches without any threshold, this internal reference to covenants is unreconciled and could be argued either way.
judgments.clause_name: Section 8.03 Limitations on Indemnification for Breaches of Representations and Warranties

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but carefully sequenced procedure with concrete deadlines and a one-counsel cap; "reasonably and promptly" is the only soft term and it is expressly cured by subsection (c).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with Sections 8.04(b)–(c) and Section 8.03's deductible carve-out ("regardless of the Deductible"); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mechanical notice-of-sums-due step triggered by defined events; the wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Sections 8.04(a) and (c) and with the arbitration references elsewhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prejudice standard ("actual loss and prejudice") is a familiar and reasonably determinate qualification of the notice requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly softens Section 8.04(a)'s prompt-notice duty and is consistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Term is defined by three alternative end-points, one of which (return of the unused Prepaid Royalties) is itself an event the parties can defer, and the extension proviso ends with the unexplained phrase "except as it pertains to Puerto Rico," leaving the extension right's scope genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.02 says that if Clearwire extends the refund date "the Term of this Agreement shall be extended accordingly," which cannot be squared with this section's bar on extending the Term beyond the events in clauses (2) and (3), and Sections 1.02(d) and 9.03 add further conflicting answers on post-Term Option survival.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Event of Default" requires failure to perform a "material obligation" plus circumstances "where such failure results in the inability of the other party to exercise its full rights," a doubly qualified and vague trigger; the second sentence about a "Loss" defined only in the IUA is unrelated to defaults.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.01(ii)–(iii) hinge termination on this definition and distinguish "a payment default," a category this definition does not expressly create, leaving the cure periods keyed to an undefined class.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[O]bligations ... that by their nature would continue beyond expiration or termination" is a self-referential survival test with no list, and the parenthetical "(or would have occurred, if Licensee complied in full ...)" creates a hypothetical trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves Options and ROFRs after termination, while Section 1.02(d) says "[a]ny outstanding Options shall lapse automatically upon the expiration of the Term" — a direct pull between the two provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated tax list closes with "or similar fees or taxes or governmental charges," a catch-all whose reach after specifics such as "real estate transfer" is open to argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps Section 7.06's broader Clearwire tax undertaking without either clause cross-referencing the other, and it indemnifies "Licensee(s) Indemnified Parties," a term defined in Section 8.01(b) in the singular.
judgments.clause_name: Section 10.01 Payment of Sales, Use or Similar Taxes

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The one-year survival period is definite, but the second sentence — covenants "survive indefinitely until, by their respective terms, they are no longer operative" — is close to circular.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A one-year survival of reps must be reconciled with Section 9.01's 18-month Term and with Section 9.03's nature-based survival rule, and Section 8.03's deductible mechanism assumes claims can still be brought.
judgments.clause_name: Section 10.02 Survival of Representations and Warranties

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional integration, amendment and non-waiver clause requiring writings "making specific reference to this Agreement"; the drafting is tight and self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It declares this Agreement the entire understanding "with respect to the subject matter hereof" while the deal is spread across the IUAs, the Stock Pledge Agreement and Collateral Documents under Sections 1.01(a) and 1.03, raising a scope question about the integration.
judgments.clause_name: Section 10.03 Entire Agreement; Amendments and Waivers

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sentence New York governing-law clause with an express conflicts-of-laws exclusion; nothing is left open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits consistently with the dispute-resolution and arbitration references, subject to Section 10.11 being incomplete in this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain instruction that headings are to be given no effect; the wording is unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It usefully neutralises the Table of Contents' numbering divergences (e.g. TOC "Section 4.03" versus text Section 4.02), so it harmonises rather than conflicts.
judgments.clause_name: Section 10.05 Table of Contents and Headings

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanics are definite, but both Clearwire facsimile numbers carry a California area code for Kirkland, Washington addresses, and the deemed-given rule is stated for delivery while facsimile transmission is described as mandatory for copy recipients.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the many written-notice requirements (Sections 1.02(b), 1.04, 7.03, 9.01) and no other provision sets a different notice rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]o the extent possible, allow the other Party reasonable time to comment" is a soft qualifier, but the consent requirement and the legal-requirement exception are clearly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside Section 7.05's covenant not to express contrary views to regulators or the public, which is compatible; and no confidentiality section survives in this instrument to conflict with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is unusually terse — "the balance of this Agreement shall remain in effect" — with no reformation or essential-term proviso, so its effect where a core provision (say the Option price cap) fails is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Given the recital that the IUAs "would not have been executed but for all of the elements of the Total Consideration," blanket severability is in some tension with the bargain's stated indivisibility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section is headed "Binding Effect; Assignment" but contains no assignment provision at all, only a reference to "permitted assigns" — a gap between heading and text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "[P]ermitted assigns" is nowhere defined; Section 7.04 addresses only FCC-licence and affiliate transfers by Licensee and says nothing about Clearwire's assignment, so the instrument as a whole leaves assignability unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The stipulation that "monetary damages alone will not be adequate" combined with cumulative-remedies language is standard, and "[n]otwithstanding any other provision herein" makes the priority explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.11(a) declares the Dispute Resolution Procedures "their sole means of" resolving disputes, which pulls against an unqualified right to obtain specific performance and any other remedy at law or in equity — the same mandatory/permissive tension a court parsed in the worked example.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision breaks off mid-sentence at "as their sole means of," so its operative scope is literally incomplete, and "sole means" of resolving "disputes arising out of this Agreement" is the very phrase courts parse for mandatory versus permissive effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against Section 10.10's "[n]otwithstanding any other provision herein" cumulative-remedies clause and against the arbitration references in Sections 1.04 and 3.03(b), which assume a procedure this section does not fully supply here.
